description: Narrative findings from the xebench cross-engine benchmark, published as data so consumers render the lab's wording verbatim and never re-word a claim. Schema: data/findings.schema.json.

findings.headline: Correction: LiteRT-LM on NPU is not blocked upstream. It runs, but must be assembled by hand, and one published bundle gives wrong output
findings.deck: We previously said Google withholds the libraries LiteRT-LM needs to run on a Qualcomm NPU. That was wrong: they are published. Our app was not bundling the dispatch library, and the other library was in the LiteRT-LM repository all along. NPU and GPU both ran in our 2026-10-17 spikes, but neither is measured on this board yet.
claims: Correction (2026-10-17): this finding previously said that no third party could run LiteRT-LM on a Qualcomm NPU, because Google withholds two prebuilt bridge libraries (libLiteRtDispatch_Qualcomm.so, libGemmaModelConstraintProvider.so). That conclusion was wrong.

Both libraries are published. Google has attached per-architecture dispatch libraries to LiteRT GitHub releases since v2.1.0rc1 (2025-11). They are also on Google Maven as com.google.ai.edge.litert:litert-npu-runtime-qualcomm (2.3.0, published 2026-10-06). libGemmaModelConstraintProvider.so has been committed in the LiteRT-LM repository under prebuilt/android_arm64/ since 2025-12.

Our July 2026 NPU failure (SIGABRT: 'No dispatch library found' / 'No usable Dispatch runtime found') happened because our app did not bundle the published dispatch library. We had misattributed it to a missing Hexagon v73 skel.

In 2026-10-17 spikes, Gemma 3 1B ran on the NPU of a Galaxy S23 (Snapdragon SM8550, Hexagon v73) and a POCO F8 Ultra (SM8850, Hexagon v81). The stack was litertlm-android 0.18.0, litert-npu-runtime-qualcomm 2.3.0, QAIRT 2.50.0.260828 (public download) and <uses-native-library> manifest declarations. It also ran with our July version, LiteRT-LM 0.14.0, using Google's prebuilt dispatch library from the LiteRT v2.1.6 release (2026-07-02).

The remaining friction is integration. The integrator assembles four artifacts by hand, and the dispatch library's ABI must match the LITERT_REF of the LiteRT-LM release. A mismatch logs 'Unsupported dispatch runtime version'. On LiteRT-LM 0.14.0 that is a native abort, and on 0.18.0 the Kotlin API reports only a generic 'Failed to create engine'.

The remaining upstream problem is correctness. On the Galaxy S23, Google's published SM8550 Gemma 3 1B NPU bundle (built with QAIRT 2.34.0) produces degenerate output for prompts longer than one 128-token prefill chunk (LiteRT-LM #3508). The SM8850 bundle (QAIRT 2.44) passed our three-prompt output check on the F8 Ultra, and CPU and GPU output is correct on both phones.
These were single-run spikes, not benchmark rows. This board does not yet publish any LiteRT-LM NPU measurement.

steps.label: Dispatch library is published (our July build did not bundle it)
steps.detail: litert-npu-runtime-qualcomm on Google Maven; litert_npu_runtime_libraries.zip on LiteRT releases

steps.label: QAIRT 2.50.0.260828 matched to litertlm-android 0.18.0
steps.detail: QAIRT and dispatch lib must match the release's LITERT_REF

steps.label: NPU engine runs on S23 (SM8550) and F8 Ultra (SM8850)
F8 Ultra output passes our check (SM8850 bundle)
S23 output wrong past one 128-token prefill chunk (SM8550 bundle, LiteRT-LM #3508)

findings.resolution: LiteRT-LM NPU rows will appear here once they pass an output-correctness check. The S23 stays off the board until the SM8550 bundle bug (LiteRT-LM #3508) is fixed or a correct bundle is published.
